title: refactor(ci): consolidate workflows, centralize caching, and standardize release automation
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Reduce duplication across GitHub Actions workflows, improve cache hit rates, and unify release automation to decrease CI maintenance and speed up pipeline execution. Summary of changes: - Replace multiple repo-specific workflows with reusable workflow templates under .github/workflows/reusable/*. - Introduce a consolidated ci.yml that dispatches lint/test/build matrices using reusable jobs; split lint and unit test matrices so failures are isolated. - Upgrade Node runtime pin to 20.x where applicable and centralize Node tool setup to a reusable job to avoid version skew. - Add action-level and repository-level cache keys (yarn/npm, build cache, docker layers) and a small helper script to compute deterministic cache keys. - Consolidate release automation into a single release.yml using a reusable 'release' job that supports draft releases, changelog generation (conventional commits), and optional notarization step for private build artifacts. - Clean up deprecated workflows (old-release, legacy-ci-matrix) and remove no-longer-used self-hosted runner labels. - Minor package.json devDependency bumps (actions-toolkit, semantic-release plugin) and updated GH action versions. Checklist: - [x] Reusable workflows authored and covered by unit smoke runs - [x] Node runtime and action versions updated - [x] Cache keys verified locally and in CI - [x] Release flow tested on a release-candidate tag - [x] Docs updated (.github/README.md) Rollback plan: revert head branch or re-enable legacy workflows if intermittent failures surface; release job guarded by canary tag and required approvals.
commits_summary: feat(ci): add reusable workflow templates; chore(ci): consolidate ci.yml to use reusable jobs; fix(ci): cache key deterministic helper; chore(release): add reusable release job; chore(deps): bump semantic-release plugin; docs: update .github/README.md
review_comments: Evan: Can we ensure semantic-release config is only applied for main -> release flow? I don't want accidental publishes from forks. -- response: added guard to release job and required workflows to run only on protected branches and tags.

Nina: The Docker cache step looks promising but may be flaky on GH-hosted runners; suggest adding fallback using GitHub Container Registry layer caching. -- response: added conditional fallback and documented expected cache miss behavior.
Kai: Please confirm Node 20 upgrade doesn't break any native add-ons in subpackages. -- response: ran a matrix build for linux/mac with native addon smoke tests; results attached.

Standardized release automation with conventional changelog generation and guarded publish steps.
